description:
You are a QA engineer preparing a test environment by analyzing application logs. In the directory /home/user/test_logs, there is a file named app.log containing logs from a recent test run. Your task is to filter all log lines where the log level is "ERROR" (case-sensitive) and write them to a new file called /home/user/test_logs/error_report.log. Each line in app.log follows this format: 
[YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS] [LEVEL] Message text
For example: 
[2024-06-01 12:00:14] [INFO] Service started successfully
[2024-06-01 12:01:22] [ERROR] Failed to connect to database
Your output file, error_report.log, should only contain those lines where the LEVEL is exactly "ERROR" (not "INFO", "WARNING", etc.), preserving their original format and order. Do not include empty lines or any other log levels. If there are no ERROR logs, error_report.log should be empty (but still exist). You may use regular expressions to filter the log entries. Once error_report.log is created, the automated test will check that:
  • The file exists at exactly /home/user/test_logs/error_report.log.
  • The content is a set of log lines whose LEVEL is only "ERROR", formatted exactly as above, with no additional whitespace, empty lines, or changes to the original line order.
truth: Before the start of the task, the file /home/user/test_logs/app.log contains the following lines: [2024-06-01 12:00:14] [INFO] Service started successfully [2024-06-01 12:01:22] [ERROR] Failed to connect to database [2024-06-01 12:02:05] [WARNING] Database retrying connection [2024-06-01 12:02:10] [ERROR] Unable to open configuration file [2024-06-01 12:03:45] [INFO] Service is running After completion, the file /home/user/test_logs/error_report.log must contain the following exactly (including order and formatting): [2024-06-01 12:01:22] [ERROR] Failed to connect to database [2024-06-01 12:02:10] [ERROR] Unable to open configuration file error_report.log must be owned by the user, readable and writable, and located at /home/user/test_logs/error_report.log.
